messages:
Alexa P.: Morning — quick sync. We need to lock down the telemetry gating approach for the next quarter. question: which schema changes should require client-side gating vs server-side transforms?
Matt G.: my vote: anything that affects cost/ cardinality must gate at ingest. small additive fields ok to transform server-side.
Jordan L.: +1 but: cost owners need a way to opt-out per-tenant during rollout. we can't surprise billing.
Devon S.: Agree with Jordan. Proposal: three modes — passthru, transform, reject. Gating flag in the ingress header.
Rachel K.: I prefer a phased deprecation: 1) server transform w/ telemetry tag, 2) opt-in client gate, 3) hard reject 90 days later. gives customers time.
Matt G.: can we express that in config? e.g.
```yaml
telemetry_gates:
  field_x:
    mode: transform
    rollout_days: 30
    cost_category: high
```
Rachel K.: yep, looks fine. we also need a migration plan for analytics queries that rely on the old envelope.
Jordan L.: note: any field we transform must preserve a stable billing_key so downstream cost attribution doesn't break.
Alexa P.: action: create small RFC for this gating pattern, include rollout API, sample headers, and migration checklist. owner? @Matt G.
Matt G.: I'll draft. will include examples for: prefix-trim, kv-annotation promotion, cardinality caps.
Devon S.: ops note: we should add a fast-path in the router to tag gated events so we can toggle transforms without a cold deploy.
sre-bot: Warning — last experimental deploy with unbounded tag caused a 37% spike in ingestion index size. Recommend pre-prod load test. :warning:
Jordan L.: good call. add a perf test to the RFC and a cost-estimate table (ingest tokens, storage delta).
Rachel K.: for SLOs we need a fallback: if transform fails, route to a quarantine topic and surface a pager with sampling info.
Alexa P.: decision checkpoint: RFC draft by Thu COB, perf test plan attached, and we run a small canary in staging next week.
Matt G.: noted. will ping teams for sample datasets.
Devon S.: quick question re: telemetry headers — should we reuse existing `X-Rdwd-Telemetry` or introduce `X-Rdwd-Gate`?
Jordan L.: prefer single header with a JSON blob to avoid header explosion: `X-Rdwd-Telemetry: {"gate":"field_x","mode":"opt-in"}`
Rachel K.: +1 but document size limits — ensure router validates max header length.
Alexa P.: ok, last: who owns the backfill if we transform server-side and need old results reproduced?
Matt G.: product-metrics team owns backfill by default; we'll add a cost-credit estimate step in the RFC so billing can approve.
Alexa P.: perfect. thanks all. short follow-up: after RFC lands we'll schedule a 30m sync to sign the gating matrix. :slightly_smiling_face:
